items.title: State of Drupal DevOps
items.full_description:
The State of Drupal DevOps was first presented by Kris Buytaert at the 2011 Munich Drupalcon. Data has been collected and expanded to help the Drupal community understand DevOps and measure its impact. The survey was reopened for Drupalcon Amsterdam.

DevOps represents "a cultural conversation supported by technology." Though difficult to define precisely, it has become central to technical strategy. For leadership, it promises solutions to internal software challenges while maintaining balance among various organizational departments. Developers gain system control and improved integration methods. Operations achieves consistency and predictability.

This session examines DevOps' significance to Drupal, evaluating what works within the community and identifying gaps. It addresses fragmentation in the space and encourages forward-thinking dialogue. When properly implemented, DevOps enables organizations to shift focus from technical delivery challenges toward their core message—a significant paradigm change with substantial organizational implications.

items.title: Twig and the new Drupal 8 Theme System
items.full_description:
Drupal 8 will have a fancy new template engine (Twig) and a simplified theme layer. This session demonstrates the new syntax and practical applications for everyday work.

The content covers several key areas: a high-level overview of theme system changes in Drupal 8, the advantages enabled by Twig as the templating engine, using theme hook suggestions to reduce custom code, and the phases of the theme system where modifications can be made.

The session targets two audiences: theme developers learning to create custom themes with consistency and straightforwardness, and module maintainers adapting their code for Drupal 8 compatibility.

items.title: Constructive Conflict Resolution
items.full_description:
Conflict can be constructive.

Testing ideas by challenging them with alternatives is a useful process. But it can be uncomfortable and confronting for many people.

We value consensus. This is one of the Drupal community's great strengths. However, when consensus can't be reached, valuable time and energy is wasted. Contributions are left to languish forgotten in an issue queue.

This session will outline the types of conflict we encounter in the Drupal community, and explore some techniques for using conflict as a positive force for moving issues forward and avoiding stagnation.

Let's discuss how we can build a culture of respect to embrace the positive aspects of conflict and work together better.

items.title: Drupal 8: The Crash Course
items.full_description:
One of the most widely-used and mature Content Management Systems on the planet, Drupal runs more than one in fifty websites in the world. However, it has always been something of an odd duck, with an architecture and design very different than anything else in PHP.

Enter Drupal 8: Almost a complete rewrite under the hood, Drupal 8 is a modern, PHP 5.4-boasting, REST-capable, object-oriented powerhouse. Now leveraging 3rd party components from no less than 9 different projects, Drupal 8 aims to be the premiere Content Management Platform for PHP.

But how do you use all this new-fangled stuff? This session will provide a walkthrough of Drupal's key systems and APIs, intended to give developers a taste of what building modules with Drupal 8 will be like.

Prior familiarity with Drupal 7 is helpful but will not be assumed.

items.title: Panels, Display Suite, and Context - oh my!
items.full_description:
Drupal offers multiple layout modules that serve different purposes. The session explores how Display Suite, Context, Panels, and core's built-in template/block system each have distinct strengths and weaknesses.

Rather than choosing one approach, the presentation demonstrates how combining these systems can optimize results. It covers major layout concepts, extensions like Panelizer and Field Group, and real-world case studies showing how integrated approaches improve maintainability while reducing setup time.

Attendees will gain practical understanding of when to apply each layout system and techniques for leveraging them together effectively.

items.title: Leaping the Hurdles to Growing your Drupal agency
items.full_description:
The average Drupal agency has approximately 15 to 18 employees, yet many owners struggle to grow past this threshold. This session explores why an invisible barrier exists at the 18-employee mark and what causes agencies to fail when reaching 25 employees, often resulting in downsizing back to 12 staff members.

Michel van Velde, founder of One Shoe, shares how to overcome these growth hurdles through appropriate management and leadership capabilities. The presentation covers essential skills for transitioning from creative founder to corporate leader, including human resources management, sales competencies, and financial implications of scaling.

Van Velde demonstrates how he grew his agency to over 40 employees internationally without external investment, offering practical insights into avoiding common pitfalls associated with agency expansion.

items.title: (Re)discovering the SPL
items.full_description: The Standard PHP Library (SPL) might be one of the most powerful, yet the most unused part of PHP, but you are one of those lucky developers who have discovered it! But now what? The lack of documentation about SPL makes it that a lot users don't really harvest the power that SPL brings. During this presentation I will dive into the numerous iterators, data-structures and interfaces that SPL defines and when & how to implement them in your own projects, but we will talk about the edge-cases as well, as in SPL land things don't always are what they seem.

items.title: Between structure and flexibility: Drupal for Marketers
items.full_description:
Purchasing content management and digital experience management systems increasingly becomes the responsibility of the marketing department. The involvement of the IT department decreases.

Business and functional requirements take the upper hand over technical requirements. Marketers demand a higher degree of flexibility but they don't want the technical complexities.

Drupal is a system which is built mainly by engineers. It has a highly technical background. Its focus lies not on usability or features for web masters, but more on technical excellence.

Implementing Drupal for marketing purposes means striking a balance between reducing technical aspects of the system and giving marketers enough flexibility to develop great digital experiences.

In this session, we will explain the shift in the decision-making process and introduce a tried-and-true way of building Drupal websites for marketing purposes. This session clarifies the ins and outs of our solution. It explains how marketers can use the system in their daily job.

Topics Covered:
- Shift of the decision-making process to marketing
- Working with people in multiple disciplines
- Component based content management and page building
- Content modelling and reuse
- Personalisation
- A/B testing

Attending this session is highly recommended for marketers, sales people and decision makers. Technical profiles or analysts will also be intrigued by the techniques and ideas discussed.

items.title: Drupal 8: Undercover Initiatives
items.full_description:
Drupal 8 core initiatives established a new development methodology that effectively focused contributions toward major release objectives. Initiatives like "Views in core," "Multilingual," "Configuration management," "Web services," "Blocks & layouts," and "Mobile" achieved significant milestones.

However, numerous behind-the-scenes efforts produced major changes not covered by formal initiatives. This session examines overlooked but important modifications, including alterations to menu systems, field and entity API changes, actions, newly integrated modules, and removed features.

The presentation targets site builders and developers seeking deeper understanding of Drupal 8's internal transformations and their practical implications for project development approaches.

items.title: The Myth of the Meerkat
items.full_description:
Proponents of open source technologies, especially Drupal, understand the collective effort required to achieve ambitious goals through shared vision, team collaboration and community. The question arises: do those implementing such technologies apply similar approaches to their own projects?

This session examines whether self-organising teams are realistic in commercial or public sector Drupal services environments, and explores what factors enable their success. Key topics include:

- Balancing individual personalities and behaviors for optimal outcomes
- Distributed leadership versus command and control management
- Determining appropriate process levels that support without hindering teams
- How commercial pressures affect organizational self-direction
- Recruitment strategies for self-organising teams
- Organizational culture's impact on motivation
- Whether agile methodology combined with self-organising teams ensures project success

The presentation includes "tales of Machiavellian treachery, brutal politics and cute furry animals" while examining if this approach represents genuine solutions or aspirational thinking for Drupal projects.

items.title: Recognising achievements with Open Badges
items.full_description:
Learning is something that we all do; every day of our lives. The things we learn from, and the organisations that validate our learning and recognise our other contributions, are as diverse as the lives we lead.

As people's careers and experiences become more diverse over time, there is a growing desire to collate evidence of achievements and contributions in one place.

I've recently been working on a project where we have implemented Mozilla Open Badges (@openbadges) into a website providing Continuing Professional Development in pain management for Health Professionals.

I'll look at learning in general, how we came to use Open Badges as an evidence option (and why it is just an option), the technology decisions made and the lessons we learned along the way.

Finally, I'll discuss why I think something similar is important to the Drupal community, especially as now some major Drupal companies are offering certification that I believe should actually appear on our drupal.org profiles, and how I would like to get involved in making it happen.

Having drupal.org behave as both an Open Badges issuer and a displayer allows us to recognise the myriad ways people contribute to the Drupal Community and allows other Drupal-related organisations, such as DrupalCamps, to show recognition to the community right on members' profile pages.

items.title: Models & Service Layers
items.full_description:
Models, sure. That's all part of MVC. Those are the objects that hold your business logic. Except…do they really? In PHP, the norm is to have an anemic domain model. Even if you want to move away from that (whatever it is), how do you do it? In this talk, we'll look at different schools of thought for managing your code's truly important parts and the impact on related areas like testing or form libraries. We'll also discuss making your framework unimportant and integrating different systems, no matter what they're written in.

From plain models to service layers, DDD to CQRS, we'll try to apply them to an average application using PHP libraries and see where they stand up or fall down. There's no magic elixar for designing good models but sometimes all you need is a little iron in your diet.

items.title: The State of the Front End
items.full_description:
Innovations in front end practices and technology continue to push our industry forward. While Drupal approaches a significant milestone with the impending release of D8, let's take a moment to survey the current landscape of front end practice and consider what it means to be a front end person in general, a front ender working with Drupal, and what it means to straddle these two worlds which are increasingly moving in different directions, at different speeds.

This session will cover:
- What is the new normal for the front end? What is our baseline for technology, for skill, for practice?
- Where is innovation coming from, and how can we best co-opt it for our use?
- How will front end practice, as far as we can see, going to evolve moving forward?

This is a continuation of a prior presentation, which emphasized that "front-end practice has evolved to establish itself as more than the equal of back-end, with its own robust and essential set of skills, practices, and stack of tools." The speakers noted that front-end has evolved dramatically during Drupal 7's lifecycle, creating entirely new areas of practice while Drupal remained relatively stable. They highlighted how design frameworks and decoupled MVC frameworks represent front-end driving innovation in both Drupal and the broader web ecosystem.

items.title: CKEditor in Drupal 8
items.full_description:
Drupal 8 will finally be shipped with a default WYSIWYG editor: CKEditor. Content creation represents a core function in content management systems, making editor proficiency essential for site administrators and creators.

This presentation explores CKEditor integration within Drupal 8 while demonstrating how developers can extend the editor's capabilities through custom features.

Topics covered:
- Limitations of prior Drupal WYSIWYG solutions
- New capabilities in CKEditor and Text Editor modules
- Advanced Content Filtering and its implementation
- Widget functionality and image handling
- Custom plugin development and configuration expansion
- Content security considerations
- System migration strategies

items.title: Turning Drupal Into a Machine for Automated Deployment
items.full_description:
Acquia Search is a hosted Apache Solr service provided with subscriptions since 2009. Last year, the service was relaunched on new infrastructure with enhanced automation and integration. The team built a Drupal site functioning as a deployment machine that receives data via the Services module to create or update nodes. This node data configures load balancer and Apache Solr servers using git and SSH tasks via phpseclib.

The presentation covers existing operational challenges, the orchestration architecture, Apache Solr server configuration management, Nginx request handling for load balancing, scaling to 4000+ Solr cores, automatic search core spawning for customers, and detailed explanations of leveraging Drupal modules, the Drupal queue, and PHP libraries.

Attendees would gain perspective on using Drupal as an automation tool and learn about adopting existing projects like Aegir or DevShop for deployment management.

items.title: Turbocharging Drupal syndication with Node.JS
items.full_description:
You can get far by caching Drupal's content feeds. There are a lot of caching layers available. But when you need a bit of intelligence to your caching layer, drowning deep into the world of Varnish VCL configurations isn't the only option.

We went from trying to optimize Drupal's ability to deliver JSON-feeds out with MongoDB field storage and SOLR backed Views with a Varnish caching layer to a performance-optimized standalone Node.JS/MongoDB stack.

In this presentation we'll show a real-world case, where Drupal's content is optimized and indexed to MongoDB and then delivered out in JSON with astonishing speeds with a very simple Node.JS layer.

The setup serves most of the video content to Finland's biggest media corporation, Sanoma. It's the sole source of video content to their online TV service, Ruutu.fi.

The same setup could be used for serving as a backend for high-volume Javascript applications, replicating a lot of content around the world or optimizing the UX of a Drupal site by adding super-fast asynchronous APIs.

In the presentation we'll look at the architecture, the development phases, performance optimizations and lessons learnt in storing complicated data structures to Drupal and MongoDB. We'll also look at the current development efforts in getting the system in shape for Drupal 8 upgrade in the near future.

items.title: Getting a CLUE at the Command Line
items.full_description:
Many of the new fangled front end development efficiency tools require you to drop into the Command Line. For those who are accustomed to using a Graphical User Interface, this can be a frustrating and demoralizing experience. The Command Line User Experience (CLUE) may be archaic, but it is also a very efficient way to work.

This session will uncover some of the mysteries of the command line, and unpack the psychology behind your frustrations with it. We'll dive into details necessary to enhance your appreciation of this simple tool by touching on the following topics:

* why you're right to hate the command line (and how you can get over your hatred and get on with your job)
* the features of a well-written command line utility (so you can distinguish between the good ones and the ones that ought to make you curl your toes in frustration)
* the benefits of working at the command line when things are going wrong (and why things are more likely to go *right* when working from the command line for certain kinds of tasks)
* and finally, some simple tips to make your time at the command line more bearable

By the end of this session you should be equipped to tackle command line tasks. Specifically, you will be able to:

1. create a mental model of the tasks you need to complete while at the command line
2. locate the command line on your computer
3. complete tasks using relevant commands
4. identify and apply troubleshooting techniques if things go wrong
5. safely exit the command line when your tasks are complete

Yes, this is an introductory session. This is for people who feel shame that they don't know how to use command line tools, and who feel frustrated when others casually reference them as if they're common knowledge. You don't need Git, Grunt, Sass, or prior command line experience to attend.

items.title: OOP For Drupal Developers
items.full_description: A practical, no-rhetoric session on what objects are and why they might be useful to developers. We'll start with a little theory and then move on quickly to some practical examples of what you'll see in an OOP PHP project. From classes, objects and inheritance, we'll move on to file structure and autoloading code in PHP. This session will also cover more advanced concepts such as traits and interfaces, and discuss how they allow us to build more powerful, flexible applications with less code to maintain. Developers who attend this session will be able to tackle their next OOP project with confidence.

items.title: Engaging UX and Design Contributors
items.full_description:
Many of the tools used for community work (Groups.Drupal.org, the Issue Queue, IRC, etc.) are ineffective in facilitating the collaborative decision making that Drupal needs to move forward. As a result, discussions and collaboration most often happens at cons, and must then be brought to GDO or the Issue Queue, only to get hashed out again. Progress stalls.

The issues of collaboration and cooperative problem solving are those that designers and UX professionals deal with every day, and as designers, we are uniquely positioned to help. Drupal community leadership has begun to understand the importance of UX design to the continued growth of the project over the last few years. However, very little funding is put towards UX design, and UX activities tend to be focused on singular activities, e.g. the Drupal.org redesign, or issues facing a particular screen or module.

Additionally:

* Our current development processes are poorly set up for UX/research/design, e.g. discussing design within Issue Queues

* When UX issues are worked out, "up to 60% of them are never implemented."

* Designers and UX professionals who donate their time to the community find that their contributions aren't recognized, and sometimes face negative/harsh treatment from community members.

As a result, UX professionals and designers who enter the community tend to burn out within a few years, or they just don't contribute.

The presentation will cover how the community currently collaborates on design and solves tough technical issues, a vision for how the process can be improved, and updates on the Community Tools team's work and how attendees can help move forward.

items.title: Deploying your Sites with Drush
items.full_description:
Drush is not only awesome for managing your local Drupal site, with site aliases you can manage Drupal sites on remote servers without logging in via SSH!

With Drush Deploy you even can deploy sites on multiple servers completely automated with one tool we all already know at heart: Drush, no other additional library like Capistrano needed!

In this Session we will present how to setup Drush to work with remote sites, what is possible and what we use in our daily business.

Then we will dig deeper into Drush Deploy: how it works, what it does and show how to set it up to deploy a drupal site on multiple servers with a single command, with automated backups, database updates, cache clears and even rollback functionalities.

We will cover all the different parts which need to be aligned before we can start using drush to deploy your site. We will also cover the problems we had and how we solved it and give you a outlook to Drupal 8 to show you that establishing a good deployment does not mean it will break with the next Drupal release.

items.title: Life in the Fast Lane
items.full_description:
Do you run a Drupal business? Have you ever suffered growing pains as you scale to meet with demand? Ever wished you could be a fly on the wall at a thriving larger agency?

Business leaders from four accomplished Drupal companies will discuss how they've built sustainable growth and succeeded in competitive markets. The panel will explore differentiation strategies, organizational scaling decisions, specialized service delivery, growth sustainability methods, risk mitigation, and large project delivery challenges.

Operating internationally across diverse sectors, panelists will provide contrasting perspectives on business strategy. With Drupal 8's approaching release, the discussion offers timely preparation for companies seeking competitive advantage.

items.title: Eurail.com: Selling Train Passes Online
items.full_description:
Eurail.com is a fast-growing company selling train passes online worldwide, allowing travelers to visit Europe by train for days or weeks. The company operates three ecommerce websites with annual turnover of 60 million euro.

Eurail faced significant challenges with their previous supplier regarding support, maintenance, and feature development. Outstanding downtimes caused sales drops, prompting them to seek a reliable technical partner.

The solution involved:
- Code audit and security fixes
- Migration to Acquia Cloud Enterprise
- Performance testing with BlazeMeter
- 24/7 SLA support
- Complete Drupal 6 to Drupal 7 migration
- Agile development methodology
- CDN integration
- Drupal Commerce integration
- Full ecommerce migration into Drupal

The project timeline spanned from March 2013 through 2017, including one month of onboarding, seven months of re-development, and 1.5 years of ongoing support.

Results achieved include zero downtime, stable sales, improved user experience, optimized ecommerce flows, and enhanced content management capabilities.

items.title: Drupal.org in 2015: What's coming next?
items.full_description: Over the past few months the Drupal Association's Tech team has been working closely with the Drupal.org Content, Software and Infrastructure Working Groups to come up with a list of priorities for Drupal.org for next year.

items.title: The recipe for success: BBC Good Food
items.full_description:
What does it take for the UK's most popular recipe website to keep that standing? Engaging content, powerful search & navigation and a seamless experience across devices.

The BBC Good Food digital team discusses their platform's evolution, describing how they constructed their current user experience and outlining future directions for their digital offerings.

items.title: Drupal 8 Media
items.full_description:
Every keynote by Dries, and every time a new version of Drupal core is released, one of the biggest features asked for in Drupal 8 is better media handling. There are currently a wide selection of media management solutions for Drupal 7: media, scald, asset, mediabox and more, each with its own strengths and weaknesses.

At DrupalCon Prague, the first steps were done towards a unified media solution for Drupal 8 using media entities, while the File Entity and Media maintainers wanted to continue extending core's file entities. At NYCCamp the different teams came together to agree on a common solution forward. This session is the occasion to present our progress so far.

There is also quite a lot of organizational and political questions related to this field and we'll try to present some of those also, including:

- Why disagreeing on what entity type to use benefits the solution for end users
- The challenges that we foresee when porting and revamping these modules
- Where help is necessary still in Drupal 8 to meet those challenges
- A call to action to help contribute at the code sprint!

Things we'd like to discuss with the D8 core and contrib developers:

- How can we solve contrib library dependencies? We're using Composer for Drupal Core but we also include all of our external libraries in Core itself. Should contrib do the same?
- What, if anything should we propose to improve the media handling support for Drupal 8 core before release? What could we include in the 8.x minor releases? What needs to wait for Drupal 9?
- What needs have we not considered or need to meet?

items.title: Getting Content to a Phone in less than 1000ms
items.full_description:
"We must get the content to the user, and we must do it fast." In today's fast-paced digital environment, achieving sub-1000ms page load times is essential for user retention and engagement. While this performance threshold has been discussed extensively in web development circles, the practical implementation remains challenging.

This presentation addresses strategies for optimizing Drupal sites by reducing page bloat and improving delivery speed, particularly for mobile users. The speaker covers TCP protocol fundamentals to explain performance bottlenecks, explores available modules for frontend developers, and discusses advanced theming techniques to maximize site speed and deliver one of the fastest web experiences possible.

items.title: Contributing to Drupal as a Small Business
items.full_description:
We are all powered by Drupal, so lets keep it running! Every single contributor makes a difference to the community. Business owners of all sizes have a unique opportunity to empower their team to be a team of active contributors!

At Hook 42, one of our strategic business goals is to be actively involved in and give back to the Drupal Community. We contribute in ways that are within the means of our company size - we are a team of 8 and qualify as "small". Before the company we were freelancers, so we know how to contribute on an individual to medium scale.

This session will surface how we plan, budget, and execute our Drupal community efforts. Our goal is to provide you and your team creative options for community contributions within your company or individual resources.

Everyone makes a difference!

items.title: The SPDY Sandwich
items.full_description:
We're all putting in lots of effort to 'make the web faster', and DevOps practitioners are especially interested in using tools to make their sites superfast. Nginx and Varnish are go-to performance tools to make your site fly, but with some cross-over in what they can do, and important capability differences in that cross-over zone, how can you get the best out of them?

This talk will look at using Nginx and Varnish together with SPDY in a 'SPDY sandwich' (Nginx » Varnish » Nginx) to reduce the latency of web pages, and to improve web security. With some overview of the technologies involved, their strengths and benefits, weaknesses and limitations, we'll focus on putting them all together and getting benchmarks for the potential performance paybacks.

The session will cover:

* Nginx, I got you (I feel good)
* Varnish - Bring it on … Bring it on
* Superbad, Superslick, SPDY - What, why, how?
* Get on the Good Foot - Everything in SSL/TLS, and encryption ciphers
* Get it together - the SPDY sandwich
* The Payback - testing it all

Barney Hanlon originally proposed the 'SPDY Sandwich'. This session is an in-depth look at set-up and configuration, with special attention given to performance benchmarks.

items.title: How NOT to build and maintain a Drupal site
items.full_description:
There are several ways in which you can learn 'how to build a Drupal site', this session focusses on 'how NOT to build a Drupal site'!

This session talks about the bad, worse and worst practices which many novice developers are vulnerable to follow. Such practices are followed simply due to lack of awareness of their implications or to take shortcuts to achieve desired behavior in a site.

The session highlights the practices which have a potential to bring your site down when you need it the most!!

In my 8 years of Drupal career, I have burnt countless nights solving issues on Drupal sites built by others, just because someone followed bad practices while building the sites!

This session summarizes this experience and provides a nice consolidated 'NOT TO DO' list to developers and site builders.

This session will cover:

* How NOT to plan, design and architect a Drupal site
* What NOT to do when building a Drupal Site
* What NOT to do when creating a custom theme
* What NOT to do when writing custom code
* Which configuration settings should NOT be left on live sites
* How NOT to host a Drupal site
* How NOT to maintain and manage a Drupal site

At the end of the session you will take away a nice handy list of what NOT to do on your next Drupal projects. Then, you can spend your evenings the way you want to and NOT for solving issues!

items.title: PHP from the CLI
items.full_description: PHP is a powerful tool. It is estimated that it is running on more than 80% of the servers on the web today. Many developers overlook its command-line capabilities. The session demonstrates how to leverage PHP beyond web applications for tasks like data processing and system maintenance. It progresses from fundamental command-line examples to implementing PHP within sophisticated application architectures.

items.title: Sell Anything to Anyone, Anywhere
items.full_description:
For the last five years Commerce Guys has pursued its vision to develop the leading open source eCommerce framework on Drupal. As the company's international presence expanded, their understanding of such a framework grew to encompass the tools and systems required to sell anything to anyone anywhere. Recent developments in the Drupal Commerce 1.x contributed module ecosystem and in Drupal Commerce 2.x itself demonstrate progress in providing global support for currencies, price formatting, addressing, and more.

As of Summer, with the launch of Platform.sh to the general public, the company now provides development teams with tools to launch their projects faster. Additionally, the tools developed to drive recurring billing and voucher systems are now available to power digital commerce projects.

In this session, Ryan and Augustin will showcase these latest developments at Commerce Guys with a special focus on the business value they bring to partners and customers.

items.title: Drupal 8 Breakpoints and Responsive images
items.full_description:
A session for site builders and themers to get all the details about breakpoints and responsive images (picture) in Drupal 8.

1/ A bit of history
- why do we need this
- drupal 7 version
- the evolution of the picture tag
- performance benefits
- the polyfill and some pitfalls

2/ Breakpoints
- breakpoints used for the layout (grid) in your theme
- breakpoints used for inline content

3/ Responsive image mappings
- why do we need this
- when to use sizes, when to use breakpoints
- use of different mime types

4/ How to use it

5/ The future

items.title: Open Source Design
items.full_description:
Open source becomes increasingly vital as the web is dominated by corporations. With growing public interest in privacy and security, design and user experience significantly influence software project success.

The designer community in open source has expanded, though demand for more talent persists. Collaboration remains essential.

Drawing from experience at ownCloud and other projects, this session explores practical design methodologies.

Key discussion points include:
* Cultivating design culture within projects
* Developer-designer collaboration strategies
* Bridging the gap between design and development roles
* Engaging university students in design work
* The value of cross-project design partnerships

items.title: Understanding the Building Blocks of Performance
items.full_description:
"Just scale it in the cloud" — "No you've got to put the database on raw metal!" — "You've gotta use Memcache if you want performance" — "You need Nginx for speed"

It's straightforward to receive questionable guidance regarding efficient Drupal architecture. However, no single solution fits all circumstances. Drupal, by nature, provides flexibility, and its resource needs vary based on implementation specifics. Budget constraints mean investments must rely on sound, comprehensive information.

This presentation examines prevalent hosting architectures and performance technologies, emphasising the reasoning behind their use:

- Single server versus multi-tiered systems
- Server functions and resource demands in tiered setups
- Database options: MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite
- Web servers: Apache, Nginx
- PHP execution: FPM, CGI, LibModPHP
- Caching layers: Varnish, Nginx, Squid, Akamai, Fastly
- Cache backends: Memcache, Redis

Selecting appropriate solutions requires understanding measurement approaches. Free and commercial evaluation tools are essential:

- JMeter testing
- Blazemeter testing
- XHProf profiling
- Cacti monitoring
- New Relic monitoring and profiling

Preparing systems for production involves addressing the ten most prevalent Drupal performance complications and their fixes. Monitoring reveals these problems and guides solution selection.

items.title: The Case (or not) for PostgreSQL
items.full_description:
PostgreSQL is an open-source database implementing ANSI SQL standards closely. As a community, Drupal supports running on PostgreSQL. However, the pgsql and sqlite database drivers have received inconsistent support in core and contrib. Most Drupal sites use the mysql driver, and many maintainers don't prioritize alternative database support.

The speaker will discuss the state of the pgsql driver, including two potential paths forward: moving pgsql support into contrib with implications for Drupal's future, or maintaining it in core for Drupal 8 and beyond while addressing current issues and initiatives like testbot improvements.

items.title: How to Sell Agile
items.full_description:
Agile methodology has become widespread, yet many Drupal companies resist adoption, defaulting to waterfall or pseudo-agile approaches due to unsuccessful sales efforts. Wunderkraut, founded on agile principles, exclusively delivers agile projects while successfully converting non-agile clientele.

The presenter claims expertise in selling agile to traditionally non-agile organizations, drawing on extensive industry experience. This session aims to equip Drupal vendors with practical strategies for genuine agile transition, sharing insider knowledge from "the largest Drupal services provider in Europe."

Attendees should expect actionable starting points rather than definitive solutions. The speaker cautions this is the session's debut presentation, so participants will essentially serve as beta testers for emerging content.

items.title: Dependency Injection
items.full_description:
Drupal 8 is about some fundamental changes in the way the platform is built: from OOP everywhere to Twig as a templating system.

The session explores how Drupal 8 incorporates the Dependency Injection design pattern to enhance code decoupling and testability. The speaker uses practical examples to introduce this concept, then delves into the Symfony Dependency Injection Container that underpins Drupal 8's architecture. The presentation emphasises that sophisticated programming concepts need not be complicated to understand.

items.title: COD: Effectively Powering Conferences with Drupal
items.full_description:
Many people in the Drupal community have some familiarity with COD, the Conference Organizing Distribution, due to its long history in powering regional Drupal event sites. Development of COD has recently seen a resurgence in resources and has expanded the power and usefulness of COD beyond the Drupal community.

In this case study, we'll feature LinuxFest Northwest, the premier Linux event for the Pacific Northwest United States and Western Canada which draws over 1500 attendees every April. We'll cover many of LinuxFest's requirements including session submission, scheduling, ticketing/registration, and sponsorships; and how COD has effectively addressed those needs. Then we'll focus on some key areas where Drupal's flexibility has allowed LinuxFest to scale efficiently to handle its growing number of attendees, including a registration check-in system, badge label and barcode printing, digital signage, and RESTFUL endpoints for 3rd party mobile applications.

We'll conclude by highlighting some of the recent COD developments and how COD can be used to help any organization with event management needs.

items.title: Website Success from the Platform Up
items.full_description:
There's no denying that launching websites is a big undertaking, but it also represents a colossal opportunity for your business. If you nail it, people will sing your praises eternally.

Take steps now to lock in a perfect launch and you'll find that by focusing on your website success - from the platform up - you can run a more efficient organization with better profits and happier customers.

In this platform-agnostic session co-hosted by Pantheon, you'll learn best practices and tools for rooting out problems and doubling site performance by launch day:

* How to lead an agile, coordinated launch with a cross-functional website team
* Actionable tips for benchmarking your performance and capacity
* How to increase website value through iteration - "always be launching"

items.title: Drupal.org Licensing Working Group Discussion
items.full_description: Licensing issues have been managed inconsistently over several years, leaving contributors uncertain about what can be included and leaving questions unresolved for extended periods. To improve consistency and responsiveness, the community proposes establishing a Drupal.org Licensing Working Group. This session will examine the underlying issues and review the proposed charter before presenting it to the broader community for input.

items.title: Decoupled Front-end and the Future
items.full_description:
For years, front-enders have had an uneasy alliance at best with Drupal, but with the advent of client side Javascript MVC frameworks, the idea of building decoupled/headless Drupal sites has attracted increased interest from all over the community, promising to deliver that ever-elusive unicorn: true and complete control of the presentation layer.

Its rapid expansion across the web development sector demonstrates this represents a significant industry shift.

However, decoupled architectures introduce new challenges that conflict with traditional CMS design principles. When separating frontend from backend, many established Drupal capabilities become unavailable—including administrative layout tools, contextual data, and display-controlling modules. This raises critical questions for developers and end users alike.

Key Topics Addressed:

- What fundamentally changes when building truly decoupled applications and how does this reshape site architecture and user experience?
- What advantages emerge, and conversely, what capabilities are sacrificed?
- Is Drupal sufficiently equipped for headless implementations, or does it require substantial modifications?
- What risks does the Drupal community face by not actively engaging with this architectural movement?

items.title: Content Staging in Drupal 8, continued!
items.full_description:
Drupal 8 has made significant improvements towards the ability to stage configuration. But what about content staging? Has it gotten easier in Drupal 8?

This session is targeted towards site builders where we will continue to explore the content staging solution that is being built for Drupal 8 and that was initially presented in Austin. It's a solution that brings vast improvements to sites owners that need to stage or replicate content across sites.

Further, site builders will learn how this solution also applies to broader and sometimes more exciting use cases - content sharing and filtered replication across networks of sites and applications.

And for the first time, a demo will be presented on the following scenarios:

1. Traditional content staging
2. Editorial hub powering a network of light front-end sites
3. Bi-directional (!) content replication between different Drupal sites

This session will also be a great introduction to the topic for anyone interested in joining the Content Staging in Drupal 8 sprint that the presenter is hosting during the sprint days.

items.title: Render Caching in Drupal 7 and 8
items.full_description:
Render Caching has been available in Drupal since version 7, but Drupal 8 and the render_cache module make implementing it simpler than ever. This approach enables "rebuilding only the parts of the site that have changed," significantly improving performance for authenticated user pages.

The session outlines three fundamental steps to accelerate your website. It positions render cache as a successor to block caching in D7, offering superior capabilities applicable to current D7 installations.

Key topics covered include:

- Cache Tags and their advantages (D8-specific)
- Cache Hashes and revalidation strategies for D7
- Drupal 8's out-of-the-box speed optimization potential
- Render caching implementation and common pitfalls
- Cache control mechanisms for both versions
- Recursive render caching for minimal page load times

Attendees will understand why implementing this strategy from Drupal 7's inception matters, and will be equipped to either upgrade to Drupal 8 or deploy render_cache on existing D7 sites for entity and context-placed block caching.

items.title: Modernizing Testbot: The Future of Drupal.org Automated Testing
items.full_description:
On October 18th, 2007, Chad Phillips initiated the 'Project Issue File Test' module, establishing automated testing integration between drupal.org and qa.d.o. In 2009, Jimmy Berry significantly overhauled the system with PIFT/PIFR 2.0, introducing structural improvements.

By Drupal 8's launch, the current architecture will have operated for approximately 5 years, yet the codebase hasn't kept pace with modern technology and community needs. The D8 release demands testing against multiple PHP versions (5.4, 5.5, 5.6) while supporting PHP 5.3 for legacy D6/D7 projects.

'Modernizing Testbot' represents an unofficial community effort to rebuild Drupal.org's automated testing infrastructure using contemporary technologies and industry best practices.

This session explores the initiative's history and evolution, introducing attendees to the DrupalCI platform, its architecture, operations, and features. A progress report will be provided, with potential discussion of how the platform may benefit companies and freelancers beyond the primary Drupal.org implementation.

items.title: Launching a Flagship eCommerce Site with Drupal and Drupal Commerce
items.full_description:
Lush is a UK-based ethical cosmetics company with over 900 stores across 50+ countries and annual revenue exceeding $600 million.

The Lush Digital team envisioned "a Content Driven Commerce website where the stories and campaigns of the company are strongly linked with the products offered." They chose Drupal and Drupal Commerce to realize this vision.

The team employed an agile methodology with design development running one sprint ahead of the build process, allowing the implementation to evolve with the design. A Jekyll-powered style guide served as a prototyping tool to validate designs before integrating them into Drupal. An automated nightly build process enabled full site reconstruction on development servers.

The project aimed to establish a new digital platform deployable across multiple regions, with the UK site as the initial rollout. The platform needed to deliver the refreshed brand experience across various devices while supporting both content and commerce functionality on a unified system.

Developed by i-KOS in partnership with Method (Digital Agency), CommerceGuys, and Acquia, the site went live April 1st, 2014 and gained recognition on awwwards.com and econsultancy.com.

Key discussion topics include: leveraging live style guides for theme development, implementing complex page layouts, integrating third-party systems, implementing Solr-powered product catalogs, addressing performance considerations, and lessons from managing large-scale multi-partner initiatives.

items.title: How Cultivating a DevOps Culture will Raise your Team to the Next Level
items.full_description:
The single biggest jump in proficiency, knowledge, and productivity occurred when the team switched from MAMP to virtual machines matching production servers. Before Vagrant existed or DevOps became terminology, the team discovered they could collaborate in unprecedented ways.

DevOps emphasises empowerment and learning rather than just tooling. When developers understand the tools used to launch and run their work, they gain flexibility to experiment with new technologies and innovate. Operations professionals similarly benefit from building necessary tools to solve business problems.

This session explains how a team transitioned from developers using MAMP to a cross-disciplinary group where members developed deeper proficiency with their trade's tools. The presentation also covers how clients and trainees benefited from adopting these practices.

items.title: Getting the Technical Win: How to Position Drupal to a Sceptical Audience
items.full_description:
We all want to convince our prospects that Drupal is the best strategic platform for their next project or indeed their entire digital strategy. But getting buy in from every party can be a challenge.

An enterprise sales cycle can be very complex and has many stages, often in parallel. This session focuses on the technical component and how to convince the stakeholders of Drupal's technical abilities.

The speakers from Acquia's EMEA Solutions Architects team—pre-sale Technical Consultants who position Drupal within prospect organizations—share their experience on securing technical approval. The presentation covers multiple stages for achieving technical validation, supplemented with practical examples, strategic approaches, and industry standards.

items.title: Layout Design Patterns
items.full_description:
Most current CSS methodologies, such as SMACSS or BEM, revolve around one core concept–components must look and behave the same no matter where they are placed in a layout. Despite layouts being fundamental to responsive design, they receive less attention than components. This session explores reusable solutions to common layout challenges, starting with foundational CSS concepts and advancing to sophisticated techniques for implementing complex layouts in Drupal.

The presentation covers CSS fundamentals including naming conventions, isolation versus float approaches, and intrinsic ratios. It examines both semantic and asymmetric grid systems, then addresses Drupal-specific theming considerations such as page layout versus system blocks and creating custom layouts for Panels and Display Suite.

Attendees will gain deeper understanding of CSS layout models, guidance for selecting appropriate grid frameworks, and techniques for building reusable layouts in Drupal themes—equipping them to confidently address any layout challenge.

items.title: Building a full site in Drupal 8 Alpha...
items.full_description:
Many changes in the alpha version of Drupal 8 remain untested in real-world scenarios, particularly the D8 multilingual initiative, which introduces significant process changes for constructing multilingual sites.

The speaker's team built a fully multilingual site on Drupal 8, completing it in under 30 days. Key topics covered include:

- Functionality and benefits of multilingual Drupal 8
- Managing HEAD to HEAD updates without update paths
- Configuration Management and GIT-based deployments
- Limitations of available contrib modules for layout tasks
- Core theme layer gaps for full website building
- Challenging site-building aspects in D8
- Core bugs encountered
- Why Drupal 8 is ready for production site building now

Modern websites must balance interactivity, content richness, multi-device compatibility, performance, traffic variability, security, compliance, and seamless payment processing simultaneously. This session also explores how robust online infrastructure and cloud flexibility enable sites to handle traffic spikes without expensive long-term commitments.

items.title: GitHub Pull Request Builder for Drupal
items.full_description:
At Lullabot, they developed a system that automatically clones Drupal projects when Pull Requests are created on Github. The system posts messages in PR discussions with links to isolated testing environments and teardown options.

This tool has become essential to their workflow. Team members benefit from isolated environments for testing new features before integration, which supports peer review and client quality assurance processes.

The session covers how the system operates using a sample Drupal project ticket, then explores the technical integration with Github and Jenkins.

items.title: New Wave PHP
items.full_description: With new PHP versions being released more often, and projects including Drupal increasing their minimum requirements for PHP versions, it's clear that things are changing rapidly. This session is all about the changes introduced in newer versions of PHP (5.3 onwards), and what that means for PHP projects everywhere. There will be practical examples of the shiny new features, advice on finding hosting and safely upgrading existing projects, and news about the performance improvements you can expect as you move between the versions. The way PHP is evolving is truly exciting so come and join in on the fun!

items.title: The Future of Drupal Functional Testing
items.full_description:
In the Drupal 8 cycle we have invested a lot of time into writing tests. We are now writing unit tests for our logic and acceptance tests for our scenarios, but what about our frontend (Javascript) testing?

Originally Drupal's WebTestBase evolved from SimpleTest but over the years it has morphed and transformed into a mutant beast of difficult to maintain custom code. Whilst we've been off on our island, the PHP community at large have been working together on solving the same problems we've been adding additional band-aids and bolt-ons to SimpleTest for.

One such solution is Mink. Many of us are familiar with Behat's gherkin syntax but you may not be aware that "the real power of Behat is powered by Mink." Most of the built in step-definitions are added by the Mink extension, which is a Behat Extension that wraps Mink.

The core of Mink is the DriverInterface which allows a swappable back-end for functional testing. Since Early April 2014, the team has been re-architecting WebTestBase on top of Mink but retaining as much backwards-compatibility as possible.

With WebTestBase rearchitected on top of Mink, we maintain a Mink session for browser interactions. The default implementation uses the Goutte driver, which is a simple web-scraper that wraps Guzzle and the Symfony DomCrawler component.

The goal for this core conversation is to not only have a big discussion in the talk, but to also trigger a series of BOFs and sprinting!

items.title: GSS - the CSS layout system that's 2 generations ahead
items.full_description:
So zen-grids and susy are popular options, and while Flexbox adoption is growing, CSS grids and CSS regions remain on the horizon.

A newer technology called Grid Style Sheets bypasses the standard browser layout engine, offering expanded layout possibilities beyond traditional constraints.

This session will explain Grid Stylesheets' underlying concepts and syntax, demonstrate real-world applications, and show implementation in a Drupal 8 site. It's designed for those interested in the future direction of CSS layout technologies.

items.title: Drupal 8 CMI on Managed Workflow
items.full_description:
The Drupal 8 Configuration Management Initiative (CMI) represents a significant advancement for development and deployment practices. Rather than manually replaying configuration changes in production environments, developers can now export configuration to code and deploy it using CMI tools.

This session covers both foundational and advanced aspects of CMI implementation. Attendees will learn how to integrate CMI with version control systems to establish a structured workflow across development, testing, and production environments. The presentation moves beyond earlier approaches like drush fe and drush fu, demonstrating contemporary configuration management techniques.

items.title: Consultation Models that Work
items.full_description:
With the growth of Drupal, we're starting to see large organizations adopt Drupal as a long-term platform. Doing so means leveling up the internal development team and helping the client identify project goals, best practices, and long-term resource needs.

We'll discuss our experience working with major American universities and public institutions as we tackle these challenges. Our focus in this talk will be on:

* Defining success as a consultant instead of a developer
* Engagement levels for consultation projects
* Building trust as a consultancy
* Identifying gaps in resources and skills
* Training in best practices
* Long-term relationship building
* Introducing clients to the larger Drupal community

While this could be a business session talk, we're going to look at specific case studies across a wide range of projects and budgets (from $15,000 to $500,000 USD), and how the needs and circumstances of clients affect the approach to a successful project.

In three distinct cases, we'll examine the project needs, process, structure, timelines and takeaways, in order to give a clear sense of how best to engage a consultancy to help solve your organization's specific needs.

items.title: Building A Tasty Backend
items.full_description:
Drupal functions as a framework and toolkit for constructing a CMS rather than serving as one itself. Since Drupal lacks predetermined site structure, developers must customize it to deliver administrators an excellent day-to-day experience. This presentation emphasises crafting a streamlined, user-friendly backend for content managers.

The session addresses a common developer frustration: "This is powerful!" followed by the realization that most features must be hidden so non-technical clients can accomplish their tasks safely. Using modules like views bulk operations, contextual administration, and field group alongside menu modifications and rethinking content forms, attendees will learn to simplify the Drupal experience for clients while reducing training time and support requests.

A new "Tasty Backend install profile" in development will be demonstrated during the session. While focusing primarily on Drupal 7 technical aspects, the discussion will also explore leveraging Drupal 8's new customization features.

The conclusion emphasises that customizing the Drupal backend creates a more satisfying administrative environment.

items.title: 12 Best Practices from Wunderkraut
items.full_description:
Wunderkraut employs a distinctive presentation format called Ignite for sharing organizational insights. The approach features twelve experienced employees, each delivering exactly five minutes on specific topics, with auto-advancing slides ensuring focused, concise presentations.

The session covers diverse subject matter reflecting the company's evolving practices. Topics span workplace culture and interpersonal dynamics to technical implementation strategies. Specific areas include handling cultural differences at a workplace and the power of saying 'No' alongside technical subjects like responsive design approaches and experimental compensation structures.

items.title: G.d.o migration to Commons 3
items.full_description: In this session the DA tech team will share their plans on migrating g.d.o to D7 & Commons 3.

items.title: Funding Drupal Core
items.full_description:
A review of funding strategies used in the past:

- Direct funding between individual contributors and individual companies
- Companies hiring core contributors on staff
- Consistent but crowdsourced funding (Gittip)
- Project funding gateway (drupalfund.us)
- % time given by companies to their employees

The session will discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each approach.

Participants will brainstorm about the future, considering:

- Sustainability
- Funding done by funding professionals
- How funding will affect volunteer contributions
- Repercussions on individuals, groups, and Core itself
- A central bucket and contact for larger donors

items.title: Future-Proof your Drupal 7 site
items.full_description:
Drupal 8 is coming! But what decisions can you make now on your current or new Drupal 7 sites to make transitioning to Drupal 8 easier? Dave will cover new features available in Drupal 8, and how you can use those new features now in Drupal 7.

* What field modules can I use that work the same as Drupal 8?
* What WYSIWYG editor should I use?
* How can I start preparing to migrate my existing Drupal site to Drupal 8?
* What kinds of modules can I use so I don't have to retrain my editors and administrators when we move to Drupal 8?
* I'll also cover some basic concepts for those of you writing Drupal 7 modules that you can do right now to better prepare yourself for writing modules in Drupal 8.

items.title: Automated Frontend Testing
items.full_description:
You are using grunt and your whole team is on board. You never commit invalid JS because no one can push without passing tests. Your Sass is in control because the team uses Bundler and grunt to control config. You even have buy-in from the client to choose performance over certain design elements. It's the golden age of web development!

But... there are still bugs on the site! And what's worse, you see them cropping up on features you already shipped. Wouldn't it be great if functional testing of your user interface could be as automated and carefree as your developers' workflow? Wouldn't it be cool if you could track performance and regularly measure trends as a site is developed?

Come to this session and we'll discuss how to use functional testing to spot regressions early and often, even before you merge. We'll show how you can visually diff your development branches against master and verify that nothing changed except the stuff you wanted to change. We'll talk about tools like CasperJS, Phantomas, and Wraith.

items.title: Building a Multilingual, Multidomain Drupal Site
items.full_description:
We are from Switzerland and do Drupal. What can we do really well? With 4 official languages, of course, we can do multilingual websites! But sometimes this is not enough. Our customers are big and international, and usually have multiple sites for each country. Which makes it really hard for the global webmasters to manage the site and make sure that the country editors do not break the site. So the best solution is to have only one site, with multiple Domains. We're using Domain Access for that, but it's not that easy.

Even harder it gets when the client is listed on the stock market and publishing a node too early could cost you multiple millions. But still some stakeholders want to review if everything will be correct when they hit the publish button. You need a good deployment and workflow for handling such changes.

Our case will show:

* How to set up technically multiple domains, multiple languages and how they play together seamlessly
* How we set up roles and user permissions to make sure that country editors can only change what they are supposed to
* How to manage translations efficiently and what tools we use for that
* Which project methodology we used for the initial development and future deployments
* How we handle deployments via a special staging deployment
* How the team is set up
* Insights directly from the client, how it is to work with Drupal and Open Source

items.title: Drupal.org redesign? Oh yes!
items.full_description:
Drupal.org serves as the central hub for the Drupal community, functioning as a resource for learning, collaboration, and development. However, years of incremental growth have complicated navigation and user experience across diverse audience segments.

The Drupal Association and the Drupal.org Content Working Group initiated a comprehensive redesign project. By the Amsterdam conference, organizers had identified the main personas, defined a content strategy and performed an audit of the current state of things on drupal.org.

This session provided an update on completed work, gathered attendee feedback, and outlined upcoming phases of the redesign initiative planned for 2015.

items.title: A real life study of large scaled personalization with Drupal
items.full_description:
Actency's technical team implemented a large-scale extranet supporting complex business rules and user-profile definitions. The system personalizes every page element for approximately 80,000 users with distinct profiles, utilizing Drupal's node-access system to manage visibility of over 50,000 micro-contents.

Performance was optimized to deliver customized pages in under 2 seconds despite handling tables with more than 200 million entries. The presentation covers the architecture, including massively leveraging the Queue-API, utilizing Organic Groups for personalization infrastructure, and employing Panels to resolve performance constraints.

The speakers shared lessons learned, module configurations, code solutions, and necessary patches developed during implementation.

items.title: Using Open Source Logging and Monitoring Tools
items.full_description:
Many of the daemons that work to produce your website are producing logs and can be easily monitored to produce metrics. In a production setup, you may have many web servers and multiple database servers. Shipping logs and metrics from multiple servers and parsing them into a searchable format can help you and your team keep an eye on what's happening and infer trends without needing to hop onto a server and work with tools like awk and sed.

A number of open-source tools can help you easily collect metrics, ship and parse logs, and present them all in an easy format that is usable by mere mortals. During the session, we'll discuss how collectd can be used to collect system-level metrics and ship them to Graphite for analysis, and how to use Logstash to ship and parse logs from all the common daemons in a Drupal hosting stack. We'll also touch on how you can add extra information so that, for example, you get millisecond duration for all your Apache, nginx, and Varnish logs, and can log Varnish hits and misses.

We'll also discuss Kibana and Grafana, two great applications that allow you to display and query ElasticSearch and Graphite data, respectively. Finally, you'll also learn how we use the ELK (ElasticSearch, Logstash, and Kibana) stack on drupal.org to manage billions of logs a month, and how it has helped us track down and fix errors from the drupal.org Drupal 7 upgrade.

items.title: Part 2: Train Wrecks & Ugly Baby Client Meetings
items.full_description:
This is a continuation of last year's DrupalCon session with ample how-to action items. Over the past 10 years, this proven project methodology will save you time, money and heartache.

Would you believe with a $100,000 project, as little as 50% can be spent on actual development? Shocking still is that your projects will be more successful, your clients happier and your team humming like a well-oiled machine. Get recommendations, accolades and repeat business - the holy trinity of business. Spending the effort and money in the right areas will give you the business results so many companies struggle with.

This follow-up session from last year's Train Wrecks, Ugly-Baby Meetings and other Client Calamities takes a deeper dive into the technical process of projects. This in-depth look at the discovery process can be used by small and large projects alike.

Clients are looking for strategic partners, not just a Drupal shop. In this interactive and discussion-based session, we'll cover specific and detailed ways to walk projects through from the what, why, how, when and who. Learning how to ask the detailed questions, understand the clients needs, manage the internal politics and the entire scope of what makes a project successful will help everyone get better results.

items.title: Drupal 8 multilingual hands-on
items.full_description:
Over a thousand people contributed to multilingual improvements in Drupal 8 across three years, resolving approximately a thousand issues. This makes Drupal 8 exceptional for creating single-language non-English sites and especially multilingual ones, with significantly more support than Drupal 7 core and fewer lines of code.

This hands-on lab provides practical exposure to the improvements and offers guidance on leveraging new solutions effectively. It addresses where contributed modules remain necessary.

The session suits those with Drupal 6 or 7 multilingual site-building experience, though those new to multilingual development will benefit substantially.

items.title: Symfony2 Best Practices from the Trenches
items.full_description: Symfony2 is a great framework and getting your first application up is easy. The documentation of Symfony2 is good, but there's only so much that documentation can teach you. The presentation focuses on practical knowledge gained from real-world projects, covering often-overlooked configuration details and techniques for organizing code effectively. Topics include strategies for managing those commonly-forgotten setup aspects and approaches to distributing business logic across appropriate architectural components.

items.title: Doing Behaviour-Driven Development with Behat
items.full_description:
Agile development is a big thing nowadays. Almost every project wants to deliver value as quick as possible, but not all of them succeed because of the sheer amount of work most projects require.

The speaker proposes a counterintuitive approach: delivering significantly more value while reducing feature scope. The focus shifts toward prioritizing quality over quantity in software development. Through integrating BDD methodology and tools, teams can achieve more successful project outcomes.

This presentation addresses professionals involved in complex software delivery. It explores how to manage software complexity through sustained collaboration and rapid feedback mechanisms. While framed as a management-focused talk, it offers insights relevant to both technical and business-oriented attendees.

items.title: Drupal in the Hip Hop Virtual Machine
items.full_description:
There's a renaissance occurring in the PHP community (often referenced as #phprenaissance). The Hip Hop project represents a significant driver of this renewed interest, offering substantial improvements to PHP performance.

Initial benchmarks presented at DrupalCon Austin demonstrated that performance versus a well-tuned PHP 5.3 environment with APC was increased by 50% when running a sample Drupal site on the Hip Hop Virtual Machine.

Building on those findings, this session explores the practical realities of deploying Drupal sites in production using this modern engine.

The presentation targets DevOps professionals and Drupal architects focused on improving performance, along with developers aiming to create forward-compatible modules. It addresses setup procedures for HHVM, potential technical challenges to avoid, and strategies for maximising advantages offered by next-generation PHP runtimes.

items.title: Styleguide-Driven Development: The New Web Development
items.full_description:
The session introduces Styleguide-Driven Development, which integrates agile methodology with web development through two core requirements: component-based design and automated style guides.

The presentation addresses longstanding CSS challenges. Traditional approaches have resulted in fragile, unmaintainable stylesheets with unintentional bleed across the site and specificity problems. Modern methodologies like OOCSS, SMACSS, and BEM demonstrate that planning before building can make projects maintainable, easier to debug, and smaller with reduced CSS file sizes.

Key topics covered include CSS layering techniques, design components as the foundation of front-end projects, Sass organisation and version control, and implementing components within existing Drupal constraints. The session concludes with steps for automatically generating front-end style guides to document design components.

items.title: Delivering Excellence with Drupal for Fortune 500 Companies
items.full_description:
EPAM Systems is a global information technology services provider employing nearly 10,000 engineers, with clients including UBS, Coca-Cola, DirecTV, Viacom, Thomson Reuters, IHG, and Expedia.

Recently, the attitude to open-source solutions in the enterprise world has changed and more and more clients choose platforms like Drupal for building high traffic and scalable web solutions. This session covers:

Clients
- What Fortune 500 clients need
- How a Fortune 500 company differs from an SMB client
- How to build client trust

People
- How to prepare a team of 20-30 Drupal developers in a year
- How to get together the right team of back-end and front-end developers, business analysts, and testers
- Motivation of a large team in a long-term project

Processes
- How 20+ people in 5+ roles over 3+ locations work together
- How to ensure quality of decisions
- What to do when working on 5 projects for the same client
- How to secure and share knowledge between projects of the same customer

items.title: Multilingual Site Setup and Management
items.full_description:
Multilingual was an afterthought in the design of Drupal 7. Luckily, there has been a significant effort that now makes it possible and even simple. This presentation addresses Drupal 7's multilingual capabilities using the Lingotek translation module. Topics covered include preparing sites and dependencies, translating content elements (blocks, menus, views, taxonomy, and interfaces), managing continuously evolving content, coordinating translation assistance, establishing translation workflows with automation options, and combining machine, community, and professional translation services.

The session also covers building a multilingual & multi-country e-commerce site for luxury brands. The presenters share their experience developing a large international e-commerce platform serving multiple countries and languages while integrating with SAP systems. The discussion encompasses managing different country workflows, importing/exporting content, CDN integration and performance optimisation, SSL implementation, and IP-based geolocation. Examples feature luxury brands including Céline and MakeUpForever.

items.title: Distributed Companies are the Future
items.full_description:
The Drupal project operates through a distributed community model, and organizations increasingly adopt this approach as work evolves. Lullabot has functioned as a fully distributed company without a central office for over eight years.

This session explores why businesses should embrace distribution and examines how it functions in practice. It addresses the definition of distributed/remote/virtual companies and explains what problems this model solves. The presentation considers advantages for service providers, product companies, clients, and customers alike.

The speaker shares Lullabot's operational setup for success, including lessons learned and current challenges. Topics covered include timezones, communication, and culture, as we work our way through the reality of the businesses of the future.

items.title: Spidersnet Infinity: Creating a Site Factory with Drupal & Aegir
items.full_description:
This session examines how Spidersnet, part of Friday Media Group, leveraged Drupal to modernise legacy Custom ASP technology through a code-driven approach with cutting edge front end theming.

Historically relying on Classic ASP technology for automotive marketing tools across the UK, the organisation faced challenges with feature rollouts, code duplication across instances, and finding qualified developers. The decision to adopt Drupal aimed to standardise site building while providing automation and accessing a broader developer community.

The presentation details assessing business requirements and converting them into modules and features for a Drupal 7 distribution and install profile, Aegir infrastructure for building, managing and migrating site instances, and knowledge distribution regarding Drush, local development, and Apache Solr.

Key topics included establishing business objectives through Product Requirements Documentation, pattern portfolios with Zurb Foundation, high-performance architecture, API and feed integration, theming strategy, Entityforms, Features implementation, flexible install profiles with Aegir integration, and ongoing update and migration procedures.

items.title: Open Source Enterprise Continuous Delivery with 'Go'
items.full_description:
Our goal in this session is to bring enterprise Continuous Delivery (CD) practices to Drupal with a comprehensive walkthrough of the open-sourced CD platform called "Go".

The "Go" project started as "Cruise Control" in 2001, rooted in the first principle of the Agile Manifesto: early and continuous software delivery to satisfy customers.

We'll start with an outline of CD practice principles, then move into implementation. The focus is demonstrating how straightforward it is to get a Drupal build running in "Go" and illustrating the benefits of delivering in a pipeline. We'll explore why "Go" can be transformative for agency stability and for presenting Drupal to enterprise projects.

Topics covered include:

Core concepts of building a Go pipeline: setting up delivery pipelines, configuring build materials, stages, artifacts, jobs, and tasks, with a focus on familiar Drush commands.

Implementing basic CD principles: testing and previewing on production before release cutover, achieving zero downtime releases, enabling safe rollback options, and making releases a business decision rather than a technical one.

Key takeaways: how Go's Trusted Artifacts eliminate build ambiguity, maximising test automation value with BDD emphasis, and managing dependencies across projects.

items.title: Multilingual Content in D8: a Highly Evolved Permutated API
items.full_description:
"Wait, $lang... what?"

If this is the most polite thought that crossed your mind while dealing with the Drupal 7 Field API, you want to attend this session. You will learn how much we improved the Entity and Field systems in Drupal 8 with respect to language and multilingual support. By covering everything from the design concepts behind the new functionalities and APIs to the new storage layer and the related query system, this session will help you transition smoothly to the shiny D8 multilingual world.

items.title: Managing Complexity
items.full_description:
Drupal 8's codebase is substantially larger and more complex than previous versions, presenting significant challenges for long-term maintenance and scalability. The core development team must evolve not only technically but socially to manage this complexity effectively.

This presentation examines strategies for maintaining large systems by drawing lessons from other prominent open-source projects. It addresses both technical approaches to reducing complexity and social structures needed to support sustainable development. The discussion covers Drupal 8's maintenance lifecycle and planning considerations for future major versions, offering practical recommendations for ensuring the core team can scale effectively as the project grows.

items.title: Drupal 8 multilingual hands-on (continued)
items.full_description:
Over a thousand people contributed to multilingual improvements in Drupal 8 across three years, resolving approximately a thousand issues. This makes Drupal 8 exceptional for creating single-language non-English sites and especially multilingual ones, with significantly more support than Drupal 7 core and fewer lines of code.

This hands-on lab provides practical exposure to the improvements and offers guidance on leveraging new solutions effectively. It addresses where contributed modules remain necessary.

The session suits those with Drupal 6 or 7 multilingual site-building experience, though those new to multilingual development will benefit substantially.

items.title: Lightning Talks 1
items.full_description: A set of five-minute lightning talks covering: Symfony2's HttpKernelInterface and Stack PHP integration with Drupal 8; corporate culture development through peer reviewing, testing, and customer co-creation with the Flemish government's Paddle CMS platform; an overview of MySQL's current state and upcoming open-source developments; and leveraging MariaDB's enhanced features including query optimiser, key caches, Galera Cluster, and GIS applications for Drupal scalability.

items.title: Drupal Lightning Talks
items.full_description: A series of five-minute lightning talks covering: Drupal & Bitcoin integration; the Drupal 8 Console project for generating modules in under 5 minutes; embracing uncertainty and risk on web projects; Druphpet for Drupal-and-Windows Vagrant VMs; Continuous Delivery as the Agile Successor; the #D8in8 initiative where team members spent eight weeks building with Drupal 8; security concerns in major Drupal distributions; and using Drupal as a Building Management System for architectural geometry and metadata.
