items.title: Coder vs. Themer Ultimate Grudge Smackdown Fight to the Death!
items.full_description:
Watch coder ohthehugemanatee face off in the ring against themer scaragucc in this ultimate Drupalist showdown!

Starting from the same mockup, these two hardcore Drupalists will compete to build it better in white-knuckle, split-screen action! scaragucc is only allowed to use the theme layer, ohthehugemanatee is only allowed to use the module layer. Who will build the best site in this epic competition?

After the title bout, you will be grouped into project teams to have your own sparring matches, Coder vs Themer style! We'll compare different approaches to team organisation and compartmentalisation, and simulate real-world project experiences.

You'll learn:

* Where each side excels, and where it falls down
* The gaping holes that are difficult for both themers and coders to navigate
* Best practices for site building so that grudge matches like these don't happen
* Organisational and workflow elements that help your team work together, for the best results
* How the organisation of your team members can affect project budget and timeline

items.title: Integration of Elasticsearch in Drupal - The 'New School' Search Engine
items.full_description:
Elasticsearch functions as a real-time distributed search and analytics engine, enabling exploration of data at unprecedented speed and scale. Major companies including Facebook, Atlassian, Wikipedia, and GitHub leverage this technology.

The presenters developed the Elasticsearch Connector module to integrate this "new school" search engine into Drupal. Key features encompass cluster connection management through Drupal's interface, Elasticsearch Watchdog for logging, facet filtering, automatic log deletion via TTL metadata, and Search API integration offering searches, facets, autocomplete, and similarity-based queries. Views integration allows selection from any index and document types within the cluster.

Discussion topics include:
- Elasticsearch fundamentals and operational mechanics
- Current Drupal integrations
- Live demonstration of the Elasticsearch Connector module
- Project development roadmap

items.title: How to market Drupal VS Adobe Experience Manager, SiteCore or Ektron
items.full_description:
While Drupal adoption raises, we start to compete directly against largest WCM solutions. During this session you'll learn:

- Main differences between Drupal and top WCM solutions
- Strengths of Drupal
- How to structure your response to an RFP in order to compete with proprietary solutions
- Main weaknesses of the competition
- Total Cost of Ownership estimates
- Is Drupal Secure?
- How to adapt your story when it comes to major Drupal version upgrades
- Adobe Experience Manager killer demo

items.title: Cracking Drupal
items.full_description:
Security is paramount for almost any web application. We will take a look at security best practices to keep your site safe and take the perspective of an attacker to understand how they exploit things. We will show you common mistakes that Drupal Developers make when they write code and how they can be avoided. As members of the security team and code review administrators on drupal.org we have seen a lot of code and what can go wrong with it.

Sharing our experience about:

* XSS, CSRF, Access Bypass, SQL injection, DOS explained
* Secure configuration (web server, file permissions, etc.)
* Tools and Modules to improve security on your site

This session mostly applies to both Drupal core 7.x and 8.x versions. We will also talk about some security improvements in Drupal 8 such as auto-escaping of the Twig template engine (XSS prevention) and built-in CSRF token support in the routing system.

items.title: Because it's about the interactions. (Better UX through prototyping)
items.full_description:
This session is about making the shift from documenting a design in static wireframes to prototyping in HTML, and from creating screen designs in Photoshop to creating a library of design components.

We'll focus not so much on the "how" of frontend tools, but more on the "why" this process works better for all involved.

You'll learn about:

* What you need to know before you can start prototyping a design
* Why prototypes are more convincing, engaging and "real" than wireframes
* How UX, design, frontend and backend can collaborate more closely
* How to base your (static) HTML prototype on a Drupal base theme
* What you can do to transform the prototype into a design component library
* Why this way of working is a better fit for agile teams

items.title: An Overview of the Drupal 8 Plugin System
items.full_description:
The Drupal 8 plugin system offers "a set of guidelines and reusable code components that allow developers to expose pluggable functionality." Blocks, field types, widgets, and views displays exemplify where plugins appear in D8.

The presentation covers foundational concepts including what plugins are and their use cases, how Drupal locates plugins, the role of annotations, plugin definition methods, and plugin derivatives for creating multiple plugin instances. The speaker also addresses defining custom plugin types within modules.

This material targets developers creating new D8 modules or migrating from Drupal 7, helping them understand where plugins fit architecturally and how to translate their knowledge of D7 hooks and callbacks into D8's plugin approach.

items.title: Q&A with Dries
items.full_description:
Do you have questions about the upcoming Drupal 8 release (or Drupal 9 and beyond)? In this session, Dries will moderate a question-and-answer core conversation with a panel of key Drupal 8 contributors.

This rare opportunity allows the community to engage directly with the individuals who shaped Drupal 8. Participants could submit questions in advance online, and Dries curated submissions to pose the most compelling inquiries to the panel.

items.title: Drupal.org Infrastructure Team meeting
items.full_description: Come and find out what the team is working on and how you can help! A public meeting for the Drupal.org Infrastructure Team.

items.title: Lightning Talks 2
items.full_description: A set of five-minute lightning talks covering: AbleOrganizer, a community engagement platform for fundraising, event registration, petitions, and volunteer activities in Drupal; twelve practical eCommerce usability improvements to enhance customer satisfaction and boost conversion rates; and a case study on how the educational sector leverages Drupal to deliver IT services across university communities.

items.title: A Series of Fortunate Events
items.full_description:
Events are the new hooks. But what is an event really? How can you best describe an event in your code? What types of events are there, and how do you decide whether or not to implement something as an event?

In this talk we take a look at how events are essential to processing a Request and producing a Response. We take a look at the Symfony EventDispatcher and related classes that you need when you want to hook into this process. When you know all about the event system and how you can implement your own events, we discuss some situations which may or may not be good use cases for events. You will learn to decide if using events is the right solution for your problem.

items.title: Automated Performance Tracking
items.full_description:
Web Page Performance is important. Period.

A performant Drupal Core is an important base for other sites to build upon. But how does Core Development ensure that Core is performant at all times?

Drupal has a performance core gate, but the development of Drupal 8 has shown that it is hard to enforce this gate. The only real measurement of how fast or slow Drupal has been at a given time has been provided by single Apache Benchmark (ab) runs and how long the test suite took at a certain point in time. Both are very unreliable measurements as the test suite inherently had quite different performance characteristics than what is important for a production site.

Particularly the following questions cannot be answered today easily:

- Is Drupal 8 slower than Drupal 7 in the back-end?
- What about front-end performance? Is Drupal 8 faster there? (yes!)
- How many database calls is Drupal 8 doing per page request?
- How many bytes are transferred on average?

This session will feature an overview of what automated performance testing / monitoring is and then go into the details of what types are there, what can be tracked, which problems are there and what could be implemented tomorrow.

items.title: Making Customers Successful
items.full_description:
A site can launch months late and the customer considers it a success and you are the hero. A site can launch on time, and the client's first order of business is to replace your company. The needs and expectations of a client don't always turn out to be what you think. What matters the most, and how can you cultivate a positive and productive relationship with your clients for years?

This session will explore:

1. What is success for your customer?
2. How your sales process, software development methodology, and internal culture affect success
3. Customer expectations: setting them, meeting them, and handling inevitable gaps
4. How to emerge from difficult conversations with a stronger bond
5. Onboarding, Training, Support: How to excel at them
6. Building an empathetic staff
7. Quantifying success via Key Performance Indicators: NPS, CSAT, Survey Results

items.title: Building Modern Web Applications with Ember.js and Headless Drupal
items.full_description:
As web sites are becoming ever more dynamic and interactive, they turn more application-like. Responsiveness is everything when building modern web applications. For this reason, client-side web frameworks do not reload the entire page whenever a user clicks something.

Ember.js is known from, among other things, the Discourse project, and is minded towards ambitious web frameworks. It is a full-stack, browser-side MVC framework. It handles routing based on URL, rendering of templates and business logic, all in the browser.

During this session, the presenter will demonstrate how to build hyper-responsive web applications on top of Drupal with Ember.js, how to hook up Ember Data with the Services module (for Drupal 7) or the new Web Services layer (for Drupal 8), so Drupal entities can be exposed to the JavaScript frontend for CRUD.

The session will also dive into how Drupal can be used to bootstrap the Ember.js app to increase the performance of the initial page load, as well as interactive pagination, lazy-loading and other UX and performance tweaks to make your web application more responsive.

items.title: How we Quantified the True Business Value of DevOps with Real-Life Analysis
items.full_description:
It is widely acknowledged that the DevOps movement has enhanced project quality, improved developer satisfaction, and bridged the gap between development and operations teams. Yet quantifying DevOps's actual business impact remains difficult, as it's frequently viewed as an expense rather than a revenue driver.

Bluespark undertook an analysis of multiple projects by reviewing associated tickets and time logs to identify tasks performed manually before implementing DevOps. Through this examination, they were able to measure the gains from automated testing, continuous integration, and other DevOps methodologies.

The presentation addresses the development workflow before DevOps adoption, how DevOps transforms the development cycle and its financial implications, and whether increasing DevOps implementation always yields better results. Attendees will gain insight into DevOps ROI calculations and learn where to allocate resources for maximum efficiency gains.

items.title: Upgrade YOUR Module to Drupal 8
items.full_description:
Drupal 8 is headed for its first beta. Now is the time to start upgrading contributed modules so they're ready when 8.0 releases.

The session begins with an overview of the module upgrade process and covers new Drupal 8 APIs, including object-oriented programming and dependency injection, the new routing system, the configuration system, plugins, the new Entity API, and more.

This workshop uses a "bring your own module" format. After the introduction, participants will port a contributed module from Drupal 7 to Drupal 8. Drupal 8 core developers will be available to answer questions and provide assistance when needed.

Note: This session is designed for a two-hour-plus lab format, with a continuation session listed separately.

items.title: Drupal DevOps on Azure Websites | Drupal & Ruby: Let's Be Friends
items.full_description:
Microsoft Azure Websites provides a fully managed platform as a service (PaaS) for hosting websites. The platform enables rapid creation and deployment of web applications without managing underlying infrastructure. Azure Websites already supports over 250,000 open-source-based sites and includes features like backup, restore, staging slots, high availability, and auto-scaling.

The first talk addresses DevOps management of Drupal sites on Azure, covering automated deployment, Drush usage, shell scripts, Azure Web Jobs for cron tasks, and continuous integration setup through Travis and Jenkins.

The second talk explains how learning Ruby strengthens Drupal development skills and helps developers make informed architectural decisions. The session provides a language overview, explores Ruby-based tools for Drupal projects, discusses where Drupal excels versus alternative solutions, and demonstrates real-world examples of building supporting Ruby applications alongside Drupal sites.

items.title: Semantic Site Architecture
items.full_description:
The architecture decisions behind a site build will determine its maintainability, usability, robustness, and the time it takes to build it.

Every successful Drupal shop has at least one person who possesses the skill to take a complex set of requirements and create a simple and clear architecture plan. But this essential skill is difficult to teach and little discussed, as it requires a great deal of broad Drupal experience, and experience seeing the negative effects of bad architectures.

Best practice in Drupal site architecture can be taught, and its fundamental concepts should be understood by all site builders, themers, and developers. The philosophy that makes for good architecture is based on semantic meaning: the same concept for what makes for good markup, URLs, code, etc.

This session provides an approach to thinking about architecture decisions: how to name things and how to use things consistently with their names. A site with good semantic architecture will have little or no need for documentation for its administrators.

The discussion covers many building block nouns of Drupal (content types, user roles, Views displays, field formatters, path aliases, menus, image styles, Panels panes, Commerce products) and their naming, usage, and common pitfalls.

items.title: Field API is dead. Long live Entity Field API!
items.full_description:
It is now a well known fact that the forthcoming Drupal 8 release brings massive API changes. Field API was not left behind - it was in fact almost completely rewritten. This session will present the major improvements to the way you will work and code with entities and fields in D8.

- New field types shipped in core
- Better DX for working with field values in entities
- Unification of "base" fields (node title...) and "configurable fields"
- Integration with the configuration system ("CMI") for easier deployability
- Everything as plugin classes: field types, widgets, formatters
- and more...

Whether you're a coder or site builder, fields are one of the essential pieces of your Drupal site, so everyone is more than welcome to join!

Note: this is an updated version of the presentation made in DrupalCon Portland, DrupalCamp Vienna and DrupalDevDays Szeged - a lot has changed since then and we are now in the final state of the whole Entity Field API conversion in Drupal 8.

items.title: Axure Prototyping for Drupal
items.full_description:
When working on relatively simple sites, there's a lot you can do directly in Drupal to show clients how content and functionality will work together. But as functionality gets more complex and more stakeholders get involved in decisions about how the site will work, it's easy to lose development hours on code that will end up thrown out as the stakeholders rip apart your ideas.

Wireframes only tell part of the story. To really get buy-in from stakeholders, you need to show them more than what's on a page—you need to show them how something will WORK.

Enter Axure RP. A common tool used by UX practitioners, it allows you to create site maps, user flows and wireframes quickly, within a single application—and makes it easy to add interactive elements, annotate your work, and export working HTML prototypes with the click of a button. In this session, UX Designer and Drupal for Designers author Dani Nordin will share how she uses Axure to prototype complex functionality and get stakeholder buy-in on projects while saving her team development time.

items.title: Docman: the Swiss Army Knife for Drupal Multisite Docroot Management and Deployment
items.full_description:
Introducing Docman: a comprehensive tool for Drupal multisite docroot management and deployment. Docman functions as an intermediary layer between your docroot and multiple vendors collaborating on distinct websites while adhering to organisational standards and predefined module collections.

Managing different vendors working with one Drupal core across separate websites in a multisite setup presents challenges, yet Docman facilitates efficient deployment with transparent schemas. The platform incorporates hooks similar to Drupal's, enabling automated testing execution for each website independently within the multisite environment.

This presentation covers multisite and single docroot deployment advantages, includes a real-world case study demonstrating setup procedures and required tools, and explores development workflows using Docman commands.

Example scenario: An organisation operates a docroot at Acquia Cloud with a governance team establishing standards for Drupal core and contrib modules, while three vendors develop three distinct websites within the multisite environment.

items.title: Your SaaS Business-in-a-Box
items.full_description:
You build great Drupal websites. You craft valuable modules or distributions or themes. You pour your heart and soul into open source. Where's your return on investment? How can you benefit from software industry economies of scale? How do you turn your Module / Theme / Distribution into a Software-as-a-Service product?

Karen Borchert and Robert Douglass are Product Owners of the two most successful Drupal distributions: Open Atrium and Commerce Kickstart. Together they've prototyped a repeatable recipe for taking your software and expertise to the next step, while supporting the Drupal project and playing in the spirit of open source.

We'll present an original prototyped, complete end-to-end solution, immediately useful to any individual or company who has amassed expertise, designed and built great websites, or coded spectacular modules. You'll leave this session planning your next business venture, Drupal-style.

items.title: A Decoupled Drupal with Silex
items.full_description:
What does a major media company do when they want to manage media content with Drupal but serve a REST API to thousands of users across desktop sites, mobile phones, and set top boxes? They could wait for Drupal 8, or do one better and take a Decoupled CMS route.

This session looks at how Palantir.net paired up Drupal 7 with Elasticsearch and Silex, a Symfony-based microframework well suited to lightweight web service APIs, to build a robust and scalable media metadata system.

The result was a redundant, multi-server, multi-application distribution platform integrating with no less than four 3rd party systems, including Rotten Tomatoes. Once it hit production the performance was superb thanks to its decoupled approach and smart use of HTTP; the system is far faster and more secure than had it been built with just Drupal 7 alone.

The decoupled CMS approach has a lot going for it, and the advances made in Drupal 8 will make that even more viable. There's no need to wait, however. High-performance web services with Drupal are ready today.

items.title: Vanilla JS*
items.full_description:
A practical guide to understanding when Vanilla JS is enough and when it is not.

Browsers APIs have matured, and developers should leverage them appropriately. This session examines common JavaScript patterns in Drupal core, contrib, and projects, showing how they can be simplified while addressing frequent library misuse.

The discussion covers micro libraries and hybrid approaches for pragmatic developers. Participants will learn where to draw the line when choosing solutions, with IE8 compatibility considerations included. Drupal 8 code serves as a reference point.

Throughout, the focus remains on performance and maintainability. Rather than promoting dogmatic approaches, the session aims to equip attendees with knowledge of trade-offs so they can make informed decisions suited to their specific situations.

items.title: Upgrade your Module to Drupal 8 (continued)
items.full_description:
Continuation of the Upgrade YOUR Module to Drupal 8 workshop. Drupal 8 is headed for its first beta — now is the time to start upgrading contributed modules.

This workshop uses a BYOM (bring your own module) format. Participants port a contributed module from Drupal 7 to Drupal 8 with guidance on new APIs including OOP and dependency injection, the new routing system, the configuration system, plugins, and the new Entity API. Drupal 8 core developers are available to answer questions and assist when participants get stuck.

items.title: PhpStorm for Drupal Development
items.full_description:
With Drupal 8's shift to Symfony2 components, Twig templating, OOP, and a sophisticated hook & API system, advanced IDE support becomes essential rather than optional.

PhpStorm deeply understands Drupal code, providing context-dependent code completion, safe refactorings, PHPDoc integration, debugger, and PHPUnit support. Developers can navigate between hook implementations and invocations, Drupal API & core methods, and get instant documentation for everything they're working on.

Additional features include built-in Drupal Coding Standards for automatic reformatting, Drush integration run directly from the IDE, and much more. During this session we will be working with PhpStorm IDE which has been a game-changing and trending development tool in the Drupal community.

items.title: Closing Session
items.full_description: Help us say farewell to DrupalCon Amsterdam and "hello!" to DrupalCon 2015 in Latin America, Los Angeles, and Barcelona!
